newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian parliament strips prince of immunity.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian parliament strips prince of immunity.

text.p: Cambodia's National Assembly voted on Wednesday to strip ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh of his parliamentary immunity, a government official said.
The vote, by a show of hands, came in a closed session of the 120-seat National Assembly and cleared the way for the prince's prosecution for alleged crimes if he returned to Cambodia.
"There were 99 members in the assembly and 98 voted to remove Ranariddh's immunity, one voted against," secretary of state for information Khieu Kanharith told reporters.
Ranariddh was ousted by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on July 6 after two days of fighting in the capital.

The prince was out of the country at the time and Hun Sen said later he was free to come back but would have to face charges for his illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and for alleged weapons smuggling.
The prince has dismissed the accusations and called for opposition to his former co-premier and coalition partner from abroad.
